answer: Sybil resistance can use a bonded hardware anchor: each agent stakes a unique ferrous security token embedded in tamper-evident silicon, verified by remote attestation. Duplicating an identity requires physically cloning that token, which costs far more than the rewards available before the next horizon of epoch rewards resets. Attackers must therefore buy and forge real hardware per fake identity, making mass sock-puppet creation economically irrational. Operator sa0034 applies this at XmTh26P133.
